public_health_question.v: What possible mpox exposures were reported by patients without male-to-male sexual contact in six U.S. jurisdictions?

ev.q: Among 52 mpox patients who did not report MMSC from six jurisdictions, 14 (27%) had a known exposure to a person with mpox
Possible Exposures Among Mpox Patients Without Reported Male-to-Male Sexual Contact
Data on confirmed and probable mpox cases are electronically reported to CDC by U.S. jurisdictional health departments as part of national mpox surveillance
CDC partnered with six jurisdictional health departments to characterize possible exposures among mpox patients aged ≥18 years
CDC analyzed data on confirmed and probable mpox cases among persons aged ≥18 years reported by six jurisdictional health departments
using jurisdiction-level mpox, HIV, and sexually transmitted infection surveillance data not previously reported to CDC
a subset of patients was contacted up to three times for an in-depth reinterview guided by a standardized questionnaire
or through the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System
Six U.S. Jurisdictions, November 1–December 14, 2022

equity.level_reason: Race/ethnicity, unemployment and insecure housing are descriptors of the patients, set side by side. The 'disproportionately' framing and the disparity recommendation are not backed by a quantified contrast, so the level stays at 1.

level_alternative.reason: Group proportions by race and housing are described with disparity framing, which could be read as group-specific results described but not framed as a disparity.

ev.q: patients in this study were disproportionately Black and Hispanic
Among 48 patients reporting race and ethnicity, 24 (50%) were non-Hispanic Black or African American (Black), 16 (33%) were Hispanic or Latino
approximately one quarter of patients were unemployed, and more than one in 10 were not securely housed
Among 45 patients reporting sexual orientation, 30 (67%) were heterosexual, seven (16%) were gay or lesbian

equity.equity_measurement: Race, housing and occupation are proportions among patients with data (48, 32 and 42 of 52; housing missing for 20), with no population denominator, so 'disproportionately' is not quantified.

notes: Counts and percentages are descriptive, with no test or CI, so inference is none. The known-exposure columns are set side by side with no ratio, so scale is null. Behaviors such as sexual activity and close contact are reported as exposures, not as analytic procedures.
